title: Knowledge Wiki bounded foundation
objective: Establish a public-safe, VS Code-first Markdown reading surface and deterministic Wiki Graph over the existing governed knowledge lifecycle without duplicating canonical claims, sources, evidence, rights, corrections, citations, or public projections.
hard_constraints: Do not add a public Wiki or Explorer route.
Do not globally rename Knowledge Bank paths, commands, imports, or historical records.
Do not create a second claim, source, citation, rights, correction, or projection authority.
Do not commit raw private evidence, private paths, participant lists, credentials, or unapproved media.
Do not turn non-recovery into nonexistence, mention into endorsement, or collective work into sole causality.
Do not represent automated checks as rights clearance, consent, editorial approval, hiring-reader comprehension, or production approval.

criteria.title: Naming, authority, and compatibility
criteria.pass: Knowledge Wiki is canonical in current-facing docs, Knowledge Bank remains a documented alias, and one authority registry prevents parallel truth systems.

criteria.title: VS Code-first human navigation
criteria.pass: Strict Markdown settings, a task-oriented root, edited hubs, ordinary relative links, and move guidance work without a custom frontend.

criteria.title: Stable identity and semantic relations
criteria.pass: Pilot IDs are unique and path-independent, aliases do not collide, relation targets and shapes resolve, and rename fixtures preserve identity.

criteria.title: Evidence and authority alignment
criteria.pass: Wiki source, claim, correction, citation, and proof references resolve against existing canonical records; claim-source closure and anti-claims remain visible.

criteria.title: Deterministic graph and derived views
criteria.pass: One compiler emits deterministic graph, index, backlink, search, health, and graph-delta artifacts with authored and generated layers distinguished.

criteria.title: Structural and navigational health
criteria.pass: File and fragment links resolve, all discoverable pilot pages are root-reachable, and wanted records, intentional leaves, accidental orphans, and dead ends remain distinct.

criteria.title: Privacy, rights, consent, and absence
criteria.pass: Private locators fail, pending-rights media cannot project, noindex is not treated as privacy, and non-recovery cannot become positive evidence.

criteria.title: Correction and selective projection
criteria.pass: CallNYC correction history resolves to canonical authority, superseded wording stays out of active projection, and the public case study remains smaller than the Wiki.

criteria.title: Operator and mutation coverage
criteria.pass: Check, test, graph, report, task, query, and eval commands are bounded; seeded structural, semantic, evidentiary, and safety mutations fail for the expected reason.

criteria.title: Scope and outward-action discipline
criteria.pass: No public UI, CMS, database, graph editor, full migration, or automatic publication is added; unresolved human and employment outcomes remain explicit.

human_evaluations.question: Can a teammate find Jamie as actor, his bounded action, its purpose, what became usable, and the collective or institutional limit?
Can a new reader find the right record, understand the labels, and recover the CallNYC chronology without coaching?
Are governance, correction, relationship, rights, consent, and reversibility understandable to a person rather than merely valid to a parser?
Can a hiring or delivery reader locate transferable operating evidence quickly without private explanation?
